summary: Sync to confirm roadmap milestones and launch readiness. Key blockers: KV cache instability observed in last incident, KMS rotation concerns for Private deployments, autoscaler tuning for Dedicated. Agreed on immediate benchmarks and playbook updates.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone, thanks for joining. I think we can start, we've got the roadmap launch readiness sync, goal is to close open blockers by next week. Alex, do you want to kick off with the checklist?
[00:18] Alex: yeah, sure. um the checklist is mostly complete, uh links are in the confluence doc, see: /confluence/launch-checklist - key items left are the KV cache regression root cause, KMS rotation validation, and autoscaler tuning for dedicated.
[00:42] Priya: quick note on the KV cache, yesterday's run in staging showed the cache eviction pattern still is non-deterministic under the long-tail sequence workloads. It appears to correlate with continuous batching changes, sometimes the KV cash -- cash, sorry -- cache entries are being evicted earlier than expected.
[01:05] Sam: yep we saw the same during the 10/03 incident, there was a spike where the eviction rate doubled and latency went up for tail requests. My quick repro indicates it happens when we hit a particular tensor shape mismatch after quantization fallback.
[01:27] Priya: tensor shape mismatch sounds right. Casey, any idea if our kernel selection heuristics could be flipping in the middle of a session?
[01:37] Casey: it's possible, we do runtime kernel re-selection when sequence length distribution changes. Usually that's safe but combined with the new batching window heuristics it could cause KV pointer invalidation. We'll need to instrument more.
[01:53] Jordan: ok, priority then: reproduce reliably and a short mitigation. Priya/Sam to pair on that.
[01:59] Priya: i'll take lead, sam will help with repro. we'll try to create a synthetic workload that matches the customer logs.
[02:10] Sam: i'll run a 2 hr soak in staging with similar qps and payload distribution, capture KV metrics and KV evict traces.
[02:19] Alex: timeline? can we have initial results by Friday?
[02:23] Sam: yes, i can have a first pass by Friday EOD.
[02:27] Jordan: good. next KMS rotation - why are we worried here?
[02:33] Casey: our private deploys use customer-managed KMS and the rotation path isn't exercised often. On last rotation test, a small percentage of in-flight requests failed with a 500 because a session tried to decrypt a cached key during rotation. The fallback logic worked but it added flakiness.
[02:50] Priya: that triggers compliance questions for some customers — they want zero-blip during rotation. We need to ensure that either we version keys or we maintain key-access backward compatibility during rotation windows.
[03:02] Jordan: action: Sam to validate key-rotation in staging, Priya to write a proposal for zero-blip rotation, include runbook.
[03:12] Sam: i'll validate and log results, probably need a test harness to run rotation every 30 minutes for a day.
[03:20] Alex: note — add that test harness as a CI job so we don't regress.
[03:24] Jordan: agreed. moving on to autoscaler tuning for Dedicated. Casey?
[03:30] Casey: so far we've seen oscillation during ramp up where the autoscaler overshoots then drops, causing cold starts. The main knobs are batch window, cooldown, and target utilization. We should tighten cooldown and increase ramp thresholds for dedicated pools. Also consider a short warm-up buffer to keep a small reserve.
[03:48] Priya: can we run a controlled burst test to validate changes?
[03:51] Casey: yes, recommended. Priya, can your team run a 2k qps burst test next week?
[03:58] Priya: yep we can do that. i will run it on the dedicated config plus a baseline on hosted.
[04:05] Alex: and capture tail latency percentiles, error rates, and cold start count. add those to the benchmark spreadsheet: https://docs.redwood/benchmarks/launch-q4 - please update the sheet after runs.
[04:20] Jordan: timeline for autoscaler tuning?
[04:23] Casey: propose we finalize knobs by Friday, run tests Monday-Wednesday next week.
[04:29] Jordan: ok. now quick incident review — 10/03 KV cache regression. Sam, walk us through what you found so far.
[04:36] Sam: sure. the incident began with an uptick in tail latency, correlated with eviction-related errors. Our top-line hypothesis is a regression in the batching window that changed access patterns and prompted earlier evictions. We still need to confirm if a codepath changed the KV lifespan calculation.
[04:52] Priya: i noticed a changelist in the runtime around the batching heuristics two weeks prior. i'll link the PR in the notes.
[04:58] Jordan: please link PR 4532 and the incident doc.
[05:03] Alex: (typing) adding PR 4532 to notes, see: https://git.redwood/PR/4532 and incident doc: /incidents/2025-10-03-kv-regression.
[05:14] Priya: on mitigation, can we temporarily lock the batching window to previous thresholds as a short-term fix?
[05:20] Casey: yes that's low-risk, we can roll a config flag. downside: some throughput loss, but acceptable for launch.
[05:26] Jordan: do it. Priya to roll config change and Sam to monitor.
[05:30] Priya: i'll schedule the config rollout and watch for regressions.
[05:33] Jordan: next item — rollout strategy. Alex?
[05:37] Alex: recommended staged rollout: 5% canary for 24 hrs, 25% for 12 hrs, then 100% with automatic rollback on errors or latency regression. include health checks for tail p99 and error rate. For Dedicated customers, we should offer a locked window to request slower ramp.
[05:55] Jordan: we need to prepare a communications plan for CSMs and account teams. Alex you'll own that.
[05:59] Alex: yep will do. i'll create a short slide deck and an FAQ: link to be shared.
[06:04] Jordan: compliance sign-offs: do we have SOC2/ISO artefacts ready for Private customers?
[06:10] Casey: most are in place but KMS rotation documentation needs to be expanded. also need confirmation of audit log retention policy for private installs.
[06:20] Alex: i'll attach the compliance checklist to the launch playbook.
[06:24] Jordan: any outstanding legal/procurement items that could block launch?
[06:28] Alex: a few SOW clarifications for a pilot customer, legal is on it but not blocking the engineering rollout.
[06:33] Jordan: good. open questions?
[06:36] Priya: one more — do we have performance budgets for embeddings and chat separately? deployment characteristics are different.
[06:43] Casey: yes we have target budgets in the doc. embeddings are throughput-heavy, chat is latency-sensitive. tuning will differ per route. make sure benchmarks are route-specific.
[06:54] Alex: i'll split the benchmark sheet by route and tag runs accordingly.
[06:58] Jordan: ok let's recap actions. Priya/Sam on KV cache reproductions and fix, Priya to roll config as immediate mitigation. Sam to run KMS rotation validation. Priya to run 2k qps dedicated burst test. Casey to finalize autoscaler knobs. Alex to update playbook, benchmarks, and communications. Jordan to circulate final checklist.
[07:26] Sam: small note, we should also keep an eye on tail garbage collection pauses on specific GPU drivers, i saw a correlation in the last run.
[07:34] Priya: noted, i'll add GPU driver health to the watchlist.
[07:38] Jordan: great. any blockers on those action owners?
[07:41] Priya: none from engineering. need access to some customer logs, alex will share sanitized logs.
[07:47] Alex: i'll share sanitized logs and the benchmark spreadsheet later today.
[07:51] Jordan: perfect. we'll reconvene next Wednesday for a progress check, same time. thanks everyone.
[07:58] Casey: thanks.
[08:00] [end of recording]

Notes: transcription contains minor speech recognition errors (e.g., "KV cash"). References to docs and PRs are shown as short links. Action items recorded above.
